email.body1:
Jack, saw Apptega expanded its GRC platform with Policy Manager, now supporting 15,000-plus programs and hundreds of service providers.

That kind of footprint usually means more in-market enterprise accounts than the team can cover before reps can work them, and that is exactly where deals go cold. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a personalized signal play for Apptega off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Jack, quick follow-up for Apptega.

With Policy Manager live, the enterprise pipeline target usually climbs faster than headcount can. Most teams don't actually know how many meetings they need to book to cover the new number, so the gap shows up late and the quarter becomes a scramble.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I will walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings Apptega needs to close that gap, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Jack, last bit of proof for Apptega.

Memgraph had more accounts in play than the team could touch and couldn't hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Apptega's reply rate likely compares to peer GRC-tech teams. Want to hop on a quick call and I will walk you through it?
email.body4:
Jack, I will stop reaching out on this one, but didn't want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling enterprise pipeline without adding headcount isn't a priority this quarter, no problem at all. Rolling out a new module takes real focus, and I know that stretch is its own kind of busy.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to your enterprise motion? I will tailor it to Apptega either way.
